NUM	<p>2f51_57c7</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874e00;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #874e00;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874e00;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #345ca3;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #345ca3;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #345ca3;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ar, ++, ar"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. NUM	<p>83bf_58df</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #27648b;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #27648b;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #27648b;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9d2a63;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9d2a63;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. NUM	<p>ee99_8eb4</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #446b0f;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #446b0f;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #446b0f;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #27648b;">Gene N</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #27648b;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #27648b;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, an, ++, an"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 5px 8px;">3,800</td></tr></table><h6>Step-by-Step Instructions</h6><ul> <li>Step 1: Find the row for the Parental Type for all three genes.</li> <li>Step 2: Looking at only your two genes, assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul></ul><h6>Important Answer Guidelines</h6><p><ul><li><i>Important Tip 1:</i> Your calculated distance between the pair of genes should be a whole number. NUM	<p>0cb8_f24b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006b6e;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006b6e;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b6e;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8b3689;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8b3689;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype.
